$comment: Company specification lookup for the offline 2D drawing reader. EMPTY ON PURPOSE: the company supplies the rows. A drawing often states a material or a finish as a company specification code instead of a standard designation; this table says what each code means. A code that is not in the table is NEVER given a meaning - the drawing reading is shown as 'needs a specification lookup' and the material questions stay open.

schema.entries: an object: specification code -> row. The code is matched ignoring case, spaces and punctuation ("STJLR.50.5021" = "stjlr 50 5021").

row.designation: REQUIRED. The material designation the code stands for, written as its standard writes it (e.g. "EN-GJS-500-7", "EN AC-46000", "42CrMo4", ">PA66-GF30<"). It is then read exactly as a designation written on the drawing would be.
row.standard: optional. The standard that designation belongs to (e.g. "EN 1563").
row.note: optional. Anything the engineer should see (a condition, a restriction, a superseded code).
row.source: REQUIRED. Who says so and when (e.g. "Materials Engineering specification register, rev 12, 2026-11"). A row without a source is ignored.

EXAMPLE.CODE.0001.note: illustration only - not a real code
